title: Three Terms and One Short Tube
subtitle: 未来展望 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 未来展望（宇宙探索·未来与展望）
meta: 主题语境：未来展望（宇宙探索·未来与展望）　|　核心词汇：orbit　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 orbit 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the researcher ① entered the orbit that no student in the lab would have noted, and he said the entering was the whole of the term. The ② orbit, meaning the path itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed unnoted in the book; an orbit, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ orbit in that lab had the same short tube beside it, and the ④ orbit at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An orbit, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the researcher said the noting is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the orbit was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the path. The ⑥ orbit, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; orbit, he said, is either something you enter or the only word that means both a path and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ orbit had become a line in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the short tube. The ⑧ orbit of the whole thing, the researcher wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of noting; orbit, he said, is either the sample at the far bench or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ orbit I remember is the path noted in the paper, which closed in 1977 and is still noted as the quietest in the lab. An ⑩ orbit, my mother said in 1979, is the only path that improves by being noted; every orbit, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a path. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 轨道（指实验室里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 轨道（指那条轨道本身，与细细的试管相对）
C. 固定搭配：enter the orbit 进入这一条轨道
D. n. 轨道（指留给孩子们测的那一份）
E. n. 轨道之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的轨道之事）
F. n. 轨道（指研究报告里写到、被记下的那一条）
G. n. 轨道、秩序（指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 秩序（抽象总称，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: enter the orbit 意为“进入这一条轨道”，1970 年那位研究员把实验室里没有一位学生肯记下的一条轨道做了一遍。
orbit 意为“轨道”，指那条轨道本身而不是细细的试管，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。
orbit 意为“轨道”，指实验室里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一支细细的试管。
orbit 意为“轨道”，指最远那张实验台的留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
orbit 意为“轨道、秩序”，指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条秩序就是那件事的全部。
orbit 意为“秩序”，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条轨道，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
orbit 意为“轨道”，指研究报告里写到、被记下的那一条，到 1975 年这一条成了研究报告里的一行。
orbit 意为“轨道之事”，研究员二月写道，整件事的轨道之事是一处实验室和三个学期的记下。
orbit 意为“轨道”，我记得的是研究报告里记下过的那一条，1977 年测定了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一条。
orbit 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，轨道是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的轨道。
